nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a uniformly convex real Banach space and let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty, closed, bounded, convex set. If a map $f : E \to E$ sends $K$ into $K$ and is nonexpansive on $K$, that is, $\|f(x) - f(y)\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in K$, then $f$ has a fixed point in $K$: there is $y \in K$ with $f(y) = y$.
nodes.title: Browder–Göhde–Kirk fixed point theorem

nodes.summary: A set $K$ in a real normed space has normal structure if every convex subset $H \subseteq K$ with at least two points contains a point that is not diametral in $H$.
nodes.title: Normal structure

nodes.summary: A point $x$ of a real normed space is diametral in a set $s$ if $x \in s$ and the radius of $x$ in $s$ equals the diameter of $s$.
nodes.title: Diametral point

nodes.summary: A map $T : K \to K$ from a subset $K$ of a real normed space to itself is nonexpansive if $\|T(x) - T(y)\| \le \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in K$, that is, if $T$ is $1$-Lipschitz for the distance inherited from the space.
nodes.title: Nonexpansive self-map

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a reflexive real Banach space, meaning that the canonical embedding of $E$ into its double dual is surjective, and let $K \subseteq E$ be a nonempty, closed, bounded, convex set with normal structure. Then every nonexpansive self-map $T : K \to K$ has a fixed point.
nodes.title: Kirk's fixed-point theorem for sets with normal structure

nodes.summary: The diameter of a set $s$ in a real normed space is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$ of the distances $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ over all $x, y \in s$; by the convention for real suprema it is $0$ when $s$ is empty or these distances are unbounded.
nodes.title: Diameter of a set

nodes.summary: The radius of a point $x$ in a set $s$ of a real normed space is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$ of the distances $\operatorname{dist}(x, y)$ over all $y \in s$; by the convention for real suprema it is $0$ when $s$ is empty or these distances are unbounded.
nodes.title: Radius of a point in a set

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
